# Browser Checklist: macOS Live Route Readiness

**Purpose**: Validate browser target matrix and release-readiness requirements before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-05-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all required browser targets named: Chrome, Opera, Yandex Browser, and Yandex Telemost-in-browser? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK002 Are pass, blocked, and not accepted evidence requirements defined for every browser target? [Completeness, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK003 Are microphone-selected and speaker-selected requirements included for each browser target? [Completeness, Contract §browser-validation]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK004 Is a browser target allowed to be blocked/not accepted only with a concrete reason? [Clarity, Contract §browser-validation]
- [x] CHK005 Are browser target changes included as readiness invalidation events? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK006 Are browser validation requirements clear that recording must not start merely to prove live route readiness? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004/FR-010]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK007 Are live speech and remote audio usability criteria measurable enough for QA evidence? [Measurability, Spec §US2]
- [x] CHK008 Are browser evidence requirements traceable to release-readiness success criteria? [Traceability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK009 Are backend/network outage expectations separate from browser device-selection success? [Consistency, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK010 Are stale browser device IDs after app/driver restart covered by requirements? [Coverage, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Are browser target changes after readiness covered by stale/recheck requirements? [Coverage, Spec §US4]
- [x] CHK012 Are blocked/not accepted target outcomes prevented from being marketed as supported? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]

## Notes

- These items test requirement quality, not implementation behavior.
